frequency_question: How often does revocation occur among major institutional accreditors under federal review within a comparable time window?
membership_rule: Includes all federal reviews of institutional or specialized accrediting agencies by the Department of Education (or predecessor) resulting in a final termination or revocation order of recognition status; excludes voluntary relinquishments or standard renewals without adverse final determination.
provenance_note: claims 1500 cases from only 1 named (1500.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 1500 review instances estimated across recognized bodies; 0 permanent involuntary revocations of primary premier professional accreditors resulting in total loss of authority.
known_gaps: Minor specialized vocational accreditors occasionally lose recognition, but primary tier-one professional standard-setters virtually never face permanent revocation.
skeleton: Total historical periodic reviews of major national/specialized accreditors by the federal oversight body since 1952
multiplier: ~150 major recognized accreditors evaluated across roughly 10 decadal review cycles = ~1500 total review instances, with 0 complete revocations of primary foundational professional gatekeepers (like ABA, AMA, regional higher-ed equivalents) resulting in permanent loss of operating recognition.
validity_reason: Statutory oversight frameworks and Department of Education recognition criteria change slowly over multi-decade legislative intervals.
